name: Nung (Viet Nam)
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Read Saul, Janice E. & Nancy F. Wilson. 1980. Nung Grammar (SIL/UTA), phonology ch. 2 in full (via archived sil.org PDF): monosyllabic tonal language, six tones and juncture described, but NO word-stress statement anywhere in the phonology.

sources.citation: Freiberger, Nancy F. 1964. A phonemic description of Nong (Nung). Te Reo 7: 15-22. (reprinted 1966 in Thomas, ed., Papers on four Vietnamese languages, pp. 15-22)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Silent. Whole paper is phonology (1 Tones, 2 Consonants and syllable patterns, 3 Vowels); six contour tones, 'Every syllable occurs with one of the six tones', 'Phonological words in Nong are composed of one syllable' (p. 18); no mention of stress, accent or prominence.

sources.citation: Lam, Esther. 2024. The meaning of classifier-noun phrases in Nung (Tai, Vietnam). PhD thesis, University of Edinburgh. 156 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent. §2.4 'Phonological description of Nung' (pp. 24-27: syllable structure, consonants, vowels, six tones); author says a fuller phonology is left to future research; 'stress' occurs only in discussion of Thai numerals. Consultants from Van Quan / Binh Gia border area, Lang Son.

sources.citation: Vuong Toan. 1992. The Tay-Nung language in contact with the Vietnamese. Pan-Asiatic Linguistics 3, pp. 909-919.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Contact/loan-tone paper; no stress statement (a full-text search for stress/accent scanned).

sources.citation: Vy Thi Be & Janice E. Saul. 1974. Nung Language Lessons (Bai toc cang Nohng, Fan Slihng). SIL. 47 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent. 'Pronunciation' section pp. vi-viii (Bac Giang dialect of Nung Fan Slihng): six tones, 21 consonants, 15 vowels; 'Words in Nung are usually one syllable long.. Each syllable has its own tone contour.' No stress statement.

sources.citation: Hoang Van Ma, Luc Van Pao & Hoang Chi. 1971. Ngu phap tieng Tay-Nung. Hanoi: Nha xuat ban Khoa hoc xa hoi. 152 pp. (joint Tay-Nung grammar)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent. Ch. II 'Ngu am' (pp. 15-25) has sections am tiet, am goc, am dau, am cuoi, thanh dieu, ket hop thanh dieu voi van; no 'trong am' (stress) section or sentence.
